September 14, 2026

Trump administration moves to scrap limits on power plant climate pollution

tags: climate, politics, health
sources: @aaronparnas

The New York Times has confirmed that the Trump administration will announce it will no longer limit planet-warming pollution emitted by coal- and gas-fired power plants. Electricity generation is the second largest source of carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases in the United States. The rollback comes the same month the United Nations warned that the world has passed the point of no return in some respects on global warming, and follows arguments from the coal industry that the prior restrictions were costly and unworkable. The regulations being removed were designed to prevent deaths, hospital and emergency visits, and asthma attacks.

Interior gave BLM three days to list public lands for AI data centers

tags: climate, tech, politics
sources: @carolinegleich

Interior Secretary Doug Burgum's office gave Bureau of Land Management state directors three days to produce lists of public lands that could host AI data centers, according to the Washington Sun and Salt Lake Tribune. There was no public notice and no environmental review. The lists have been completed but have not been seen by anyone outside the agency. The BLM manages 245 million acres, more than any other federal agency, including 22.8 million acres in Utah.

Warnings mount that Republicans could refuse to seat elected Democrats in January

tags: politics, legal
sources: @total.hypocrisy

Conservative judge J. Michael Luttig published a piece in the New Republic outlining how Republicans could refuse to seat elected Democrats when the new Congress convenes on January 3, 2027, describing it as a final battle for American democracy. Luttig argues House Speaker Mike Johnson could replace the House Clerk with a loyalist who would omit Democrats from the roll, forcing a court fight that could take weeks or months. Related developments include the USPS rejecting mailed ballots from Leon County, Florida over a 0.014-inch spacing discrepancy, and the Justice Department sending letters to at least 30 top state election officials warning they are under investigation over 2024 election records. Johnson told attendees at Trump's Dallas convention that Republicans "cannot and will not allow them to take the majority of Congress," while Trump told reporters in Ireland that he won the presidency three times and that the election was rigged.

DHS watchdog finds detainees held in small cages at Florida detention site

tags: immigration, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

A Department of Homeland Security Inspector General report confirmed that detainees at the Florida facility known as Alligator Alcatraz were locked in small cages that officials labeled "calming areas." The report said the use of such restrictive spaces is highly unconventional and does not align with standards for humane treatment, and described one detainee being placed in a cage after failing to comply with a lawful command. The facility provided 28 square feet of floor space per detainee against a national standard of at least 75 square feet, and failed to comply with standards covering medical care, food service, personal hygiene and recreation.

Trump says the only AI guardrail needed is a high-IQ president

tags: tech, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Trump said the only guardrails artificial intelligence requires are a strong, smart, high-IQ president, saying the United States has that "in spades" in reference to himself. He called critics of AI traitorous and treasonous and said there is a "sick conspiracy" against AI data centers, adding that China is the only party that benefits from opposition. He said whoever wins AI wins.

Russian oligarch close to Putin funded Donald Trump Jr.'s wedding

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

ProPublica reported that Umar Kremlev, a Russian businessman with close ties to Vladimir Putin, paid for significant parts of Donald Trump Jr.'s wedding, including a private island and a fireworks display, amounting to hundreds of thousands of dollars. National security experts have raised concerns about a figure close to the Russian president funding an event attended by Jared Kushner, a US negotiator on the Russia-Ukraine war. President Trump did not attend the wedding.

Trump floats keeping Iranian oil as war continues, says Iran wants a deal

tags: politics, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Trump floated the possibility of a continued US presence in Iran to "keep the oil" as the war continues. In a separate post he said Iran wants to make a deal quickly and badly, and that he will determine whether the United States chooses to engage, adding that the US is open to the concept.

US links Chinese satellite imagery to Iranian strike that killed three American troops

tags: defence, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

US officials have linked Chinese satellite imagery to the Iranian strike in Jordan that killed three American soldiers. The finding connects Chinese commercial or state imagery capabilities to targeting in the attack.

Georgia National Guard helicopters flew surveillance over private property in all 159 counties

tags: surveillance, legal
sources: @oafnation_actual

Georgia National Guard helicopters flew with civilian law enforcement across all 159 counties in the state searching for illegal marijuana grows. Aerial observations from the flights were used to help establish probable cause for search warrants.

Texas landowners say border wall seizures are costing Trump Republican support

tags: politics, immigration
sources: @aaronparnas

Republican voters along the Texas border said they no longer intend to vote Republican because land is being taken from them to build the border wall. Residents described bulldozing and trenching affecting national and state parkland and said counties were being approached quietly, urging people to attend county meetings. Reporters who drove more than 1,100 miles across Texas said they saw no MAGA hats, Trump signs or flags for the first time in a decade of trips to the state.

Texas Republican statewide candidate posts racist message about UT students

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Bo Friend, a Republican candidate for Texas railroad commissioner, posted a photo of college students celebrating the University of Texas win over Ohio State with a caption implying they did not look like typical UT graduates. The post drew widespread condemnation. Friend is running statewide and is considered to have a chance at winning.

Kimmel interview surpasses 7.5 million views after FCC pressure

tags: media, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Jimmy Kimmel's interview with James Talarico, the Democratic nominee in Texas, has passed 7.5 million views, more than three times the audience for Trump's speech on Fox News at his midterm convention. The interview had been blocked from airing after the FCC threatened Kimmel.

House petition on veterans' retirement pay one signature short of advancing

tags: politics, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Combat-injured veterans can lose retirement pay because they also receive VA disability compensation, an offset opponents call the wounded veterans tax. A House discharge petition to advance the Major Richard Star Act, H.R. 2102 and S. 1032, stands at 217 of the 218 signatures required. Supporters say roughly 50,000 veterans are affected.

Kennedy Center says it could go bankrupt without Trump's name restored

tags: politics, media
sources: @aaronparnas

The Kennedy Center said it faces significant financial problems and could declare bankruptcy and close permanently as soon as tomorrow if Trump's name is not reinstalled on the building, according to the Washington Post. The institution said Trump has offered to step in and raise the necessary funds. The connection between the naming and the financial situation was not made clear, and the center was operating normally before Trump's takeover of its board.

Macklemore dropped from Ed Sheeran tour after pro-Palestinian remarks

tags: media, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Macklemore has been removed from the US leg of Ed Sheeran's stadium tour after venues told the tour's promoter they would not allow him to perform, according to Rolling Stone. The removal follows on-stage comments in support of Palestinians in Gaza and the West Bank, including a call for a free Palestine. Promoter Messina Touring said venues had indicated his inclusion would result in cancellation of the tour, and that after discussions with stakeholders he would not perform on the remaining support dates, which covered eight of the ten remaining US shows.
